Hi all — compiled the technical artifacts and a short explanation below. I attached the raw SCIM replay tar and sampled SAML assertions (CSV) to this message.

What you'll find in the package:
- scim-replay-20270620.tar.gz -> contains per-tenant ndjson files with events (fields: timestamp, tenant_id, user_id, op, patch, actor, request_id). Each event row is the exact payload received by our provisioning service.
- saml-assertion-samples-20270620.csv -> columns: assertion_id, user_email, audience, issue_instant, not_on_or_after, authn_context, rp_entity_id, raw_assertion_reference
- token-policy-summary.pdf -> short policy doc with TTLs and enforcement checks (included in packet)

Short answers to auditor questions:
- Token TTLs: Interactive SSO issues a short-lived session token; default Assertion NotOnOrAfter is 5 minutes from IssueInstant. The session token issued by our gateway is 1 hour (configurable per tenant), with refresh allowed only by a valid refresh token exchanged at the gateway.
- JIT elevation: Admin elevation is separate — elevation sessions are single-use ephemeral tokens with a 10 minute lifespan and require a second factor. Elevation operations are logged to the provisioning service with an audit flag set; those entries are included in the SCIM event bundle.
- Replayability: The ndjson events include request_id and seq numbers; auditors can replay operations in order. We include a SHA256 manifest for integrity verification.
- Expired assertions: Our SAML consumer rejects assertions where current_time > NotOnOrAfter or current_time < IssueInstant. We can provide a short test script showing rejection of a stale assertion if BrightSec wants it.

Attached: scim-replay-20270620.tar.gz (2.1MB), saml-assertion-samples-20270620.csv (43KB), token-policy-summary.pdf (1.2MB)

—Rishi
